Advertisement New Delhi: Eighteen months after the high-intensity aerial engagements of Operation Sindoor, international defence tracking data has brought renewed scrutiny to the operational readiness and frontline inventory of the Indian Air Force (IAF). According to the newly released World Air Forces directory from British magazine FlightGlobal , compiled using Cirium’s military fleet database, the total count of active Rafale fighter jets in India has been adjusted downward to 32 aircraft.
 The revised figure represents a significant departure from India's controversial procurement of 36 Rafale combat aircraft from France. Following the May 2025 India-Pakistan aerial clash, FlightGlobal 's 2026 edition, which was published in late 2025, reduced the IAF's active count from 36 to 35, reflecting one visually corroborated loss while treating Pakistan's broader shootdown claims as unverified. However, the latest figures compiled by Cirium analysts suggest a broader recalculation of the operational fleet. 
 Although official New Delhi and Islamabad accounts diverge sharply regarding specific losses during the four-day escalation, open-source fleet trackers like Cirium frequently apply conservative deductions when subsequent open-source intelligence, diplomatic reporting, satellite imagery or unverified combat claims accumulate over a year. This is how the same directory has deducted two Saab 2000 Erieye AEW&C aircraft from Pakistan’s inventory, from nine to seven.  
 Cirium tracks fleet status at the individual tail-number level using public sightings, flight-tracking data and defence reporting. If specific airframes are placed into long-term depot-level overhaul, structural repair or upgrade cycles in France or India without confirmed active squadron sightings over a 12-month window, Cirium’s automated database rules can flip their status from “In Service/Active” to “In Storage/Maintenance”, temporarily dropping them from the “Active” column.  
 These directories serve as estimation baselines rather than definitive governmental disclosures, and minor fluctuations in active columns typically reflect conservative data management by aviation analysts. They provide neither aircraft serial numbers nor reasons for excluding any airframe from the total. For instance, it lists 263 Su-30MKIs with the IAF when 272 were delivered and 14 lost to crashes, leaving 258 Russian-origin fighter jets in the fleet

 India’s original Rafale acquisition comprised 28 single-seat EH aircraft and eight two-seat DH aircraft. New Delhi is also pursuing the acquisition of 114 additional Rafale fighters from France for the IAF, while a separate order for 26 Rafales for the Indian Navy was signed in 2025. 
 Last year in July, US President Donald Trump said about “five jets” were shot down during Operation Sindoor. Trump credits himself as having brought the India-Pakistan hostilities to an end.

 There have been  four instances  where statements from senior Indian officials have accepted the losses suffered that night, without mentioning the scale of losses. These include India’s Chief of Defence Staff General Anil Chauhan, Director General of Air Operations Air Marshal A.K. Bharti, Defence Attaché to Indonesia Captain (IN) Shiv Kumar, and the Defence Secretary R.K. Singh.
